title: Mutton (Lamb) Biryani
tagline: Rich, slow-cooked lamb layered with basmati for a truly special occasion.
intro: Mutton biryani is the grand, unhurried cousin of chicken biryani. Lamb or goat is browned and simmered until spoon-tender in a robust masala, then layered with basmati and given a long dum. It rewards patience with deep flavour and melting meat — a true centrepiece dish.

items: 1 kg mutton or lamb, on the bone
1 cinnamon stick, 5 cloves, 5 cardamom, 1 bay leaf
½ tsp saffron in 3 tbsp milk

method: Marinate the mutton in yoghurt, ginger–garlic paste and half the spices for 1 hour.
Rinse and soak the rice; drain.
Fry the onions golden in oil; set aside half. Add the marinated meat and sear well.
Add the remaining spices, tomatoes, chillies and salt. Add a little water, cover and simmer (or pressure-cook) until the meat is very tender, 1–1¼ hours. Reduce to a thick masala.
Parboil the rice to 70% in the salted, spiced water; drain.
Layer rice over the mutton with saffron milk, fried onions, herbs, ghee and kewra water.
Seal and dum on the lowest heat for 25–30 minutes.
tips: Pressure-cooking the mutton first saves an hour and guarantees tenderness.
Keep enough masala moisture — lamb rice can dry out more than chicken.
toServe: Serve with raita, salad and lemon.
imageAlt: Mutton biryani with tender lamb pieces and basmati rice
